story.iWant: to view my performance metrics broken down by role (Don, Mafia, Sheriff, Citizen)
story.soThat: I can identify which roles I excel at and which need improvement
story.tasks:
- [ ] Task 1: Create API endpoint for role-based analytics (AC: #1, #2) - [ ] Create `GET /api/players/[id]/analytics/role-based` route handler - [ ] Implement query parameters support: `dateRange?`, `roles?` - [ ] Add authentication middleware (verify user owns player ID or is admin) - [ ] Implement role metrics calculation logic (GROUP BY role, aggregate wins/losses, count games, average ELO) - [ ] Add input validation using Zod schemas - [ ] Return `{ roleMetrics: RoleMetrics[] }` response - [ ] Add error handling (404 for player not found, 400 for invalid parameters) - [ ] Add unit tests for API endpoint
- [ ] Task 2: Create domain service for role metrics calculation (AC: #2) - [ ] Create `RoleMetricsCalculator` service in `src/domain/services/` - [ ] Implement calculation logic: win rate, games played, average ELO per role - [ ] Add performance level determination (excellent/good/needs improvement) based on win rate thresholds - [ ] Add unit tests for calculation logic - [ ] Handle edge cases (no games, division by zero, missing data)
- [ ] Task 3: Create database query for role-based metrics (AC: #2) - [ ] Create Prisma query to fetch game participation data grouped by role - [ ] Filter by player ID and optional date range - [ ] Aggregate: count games, sum wins/losses, average ELO - [ ] Add database indexes if needed (player_id, role, game_date) - [ ] Optimize query performance (target < 500ms for aggregated data) - [ ] Add integration tests for database queries
- [ ] Task 4: Create RoleMetricsDisplay component (AC: #1, #3, #4) - [ ] Create `RoleMetricsDisplay` component in `src/components/analytics/` - [ ] Use TanStack Query to fetch data from API endpoint - [ ] Display four role cards (Don, Mafia, Sheriff, Citizen) using Card component variants - [ ] Show win rate percentage, games played, average ELO for each role - [ ] Add visual indicators (color-coded, icons) for performance level - [ ] Implement loading states (skeleton screens) - [ ] Implement empty states for roles with no data - [ ] Add smooth animations for data loading/updates - [ ] Add component tests using React Testing Library
- [ ] Task 5: Create role comparison chart component (AC: #1) - [ ] Create `RoleComparisonChart` component in `src/components/analytics/` - [ ] Use chart library (Recharts or Chart.js) for visualization - [ ] Display bar chart or comparison table showing relative performance across roles - [ ] Highlight best-performing role (visual emphasis: color, badge) - [ ] Make chart responsive (mobile: stacked, desktop: side-by-side) - [ ] Add loading state for chart - [ ] Add component tests
- [ ] Task 6: Integrate role metrics into analytics dashboard (AC: #1, #5) - [ ] Add `RoleMetricsDisplay` to analytics dashboard page - [ ] Connect to filter state (Zustand store) for date range and role filters - [ ] Implement filter application triggering data refetch - [ ] Add smooth transitions when filters change (< 300ms) - [ ] Test filter integration (will be fully tested when filter stories are complete)
- [ ] Task 7: Add TypeScript types and interfaces (AC: #1, #2) - [ ] Define `RoleMetrics` interface matching tech spec data model - [ ] Define `RoleMetricsDisplayProps` interface - [ ] Add types for API request/response - [ ] Ensure type safety throughout component tree - [ ] Add JSDoc comments for all public interfaces
- [ ] Task 8: Add error handling and edge cases (AC: #4) - [ ] Handle API errors (network, 404, 400) with user-friendly messages - [ ] Display empty states for roles with no data - [ ] Handle loading states gracefully - [ ] Add retry logic for failed API calls (exponential backoff, 3 attempts) - [ ] Add error boundary for component errors
- [ ] Task 9: Performance optimization (AC: #1, #3) - [ ] Implement TanStack Query caching (5-minute stale time, 10-minute GC time) - [ ] Add database query optimization (indexes, efficient aggregations) - [ ] Lazy load chart library (code splitting) - [ ] Optimize component re-renders (React.memo if needed) - [ ] Measure and verify performance targets (< 500ms API response, < 2s chart render)
- [ ] Task 10: Testing (AC: #1, #2, #3, #4, #5) - [ ] Unit tests for `RoleMetricsCalculator` service (80%+ coverage) - [ ] Integration tests for API endpoint (various query parameters, error cases) - [ ] Component tests for `RoleMetricsDisplay` (rendering, loading states, empty states) - [ ] Component tests for `RoleComparisonChart` (chart rendering, responsiveness) - [ ] E2E test: Complete flow (load dashboard → view role metrics → verify data display)

story-context.acceptanceCriteria:
1. **Given** I am logged in and have imported game data **When** I view my analytics dashboard **Then** the system displays four role cards (Don, Mafia, Sheriff, Citizen) with win rate percentage, games played count, and average ELO for each role **And** visual indicators (color-coded, icons) show performance level (excellent/good/needs improvement) **And** a role comparison chart shows relative performance across roles **And** smooth animations occur when metrics load/update
2. **Given** I have game data for multiple roles **When** I view the role-based metrics **Then** the system calculates and displays accurate metrics for each role: - Win rate percentage (wins / total games * 100) - Total games played count - Average ELO rating for that role - Wins and losses count
3. **Given** I am viewing role-based metrics **When** the data is loading **Then** the system displays loading states (skeleton screens or spinners) **And** when data is available, it transitions smoothly with animations
4. **Given** I have no game data for a specific role **When** I view the role-based metrics **Then** the system displays an empty state with helpful messaging **And** the role card indicates no data available
5. **Given** I am viewing role-based metrics **When** I apply date range or role filters (from future stories) **Then** the role-based metrics update to reflect the filtered data **And** the update occurs with smooth animations (< 300ms transition)

code.reason: Existing analytics API endpoint structure - reference for creating role-based endpoint
Existing analytics service with roleStats query pattern - reference for role-based metrics calculation
Card component with role variant available for role cards - use variant='role' roleType prop
Existing role stats display component - reference for role-based metrics display patterns
Player card component showing role performance badges - reference for role color coding and display patterns
Zustand store for analytics filters - extend with dateRange and roles filter state management
Existing controller pattern - reference for implementing role-based analytics endpoint controller
Database schema with PlayerRoleStats model - use for querying pre-computed role statistics

constraints.constraint: Clean Architecture + Hexagonal Architecture: Analytics components in Presentation Layer (src/components/analytics/), domain services in Domain Layer (src/domain/services/), data access through Infrastructure Layer
All API endpoints must follow established request/response format patterns - use Next.js App Router API routes
Components must use ShadCN/UI base components with custom styling - Card component with role variant available
Data fetching must use TanStack Query for caching and background refetching
Filter state must be managed in Zustand store (src/store/analyticsStore.ts)
All analytics calculations must be performed server-side for performance
All analytics endpoints require authentication via NextAuth.js session - users can only access their own data (player ID must match session user)
Input validation on all query parameters using Zod schemas
Responsive design must follow mobile-first approach (320px, 768px, 1024px breakpoints)
Maintain minimum 80% test coverage for all new code
Performance targets: API response time < 500ms, chart rendering < 2 seconds
Use tailwind-variants with tv() function for component variants - do not use class-variance-authority
